newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan official says gum arabic output lower - paper.
newsitem.headline: Sudan official says gum arabic output lower - paper.

text.p: A Sudanese official has said that low international prices and lack of buyers have decreased this season's output of gum arabic, Sudan's main export crop.

"The fall in production of gum arabic this season is due to problems in marketing abroad," Mohammad Suleiman Fadallah, first undersecretary at the ministry of foreign trade, was quoted by the privately-owned Alwan newspaper on Thursday as saying.
"World prices of gum arabic also decreased in a big way, thus the price of a tonne fell from $5,000 to $4,800 and then to $2,200," Fadallah said.
Sudan produces up to 80 percent of the world's gum arabic and exports of the crop net the poor African state $50 million to $90 million a year.
The lower prices have discouraged farmers from harvesting the crop, whose sale abroad makes up 20 percent of Sudan's annual export earnings.
Fadallah said that only seven international firms were importing Sudan's gum arabic. He did not say how many firms used to buy the commodity but indicated there had been a fall.
The commodity, otherwise known as Acacia Senegalese, is used widely in the food, soft drink, pharmaceutical, confectionery, textiles, printing and cosmetics industries.
Most industries use it as a stabilising agent. While manufacturers of drugs use it to coat tablets, breweries and food firms use it as a preservative.

Seven African countries jointly produce the estimated world output of 55,000 tonnes per annum, almost all of which is shipped to developed countries for processing into industrial raw material, according to industry sources.
